evaluations.label: A
errors: "Heart-shaped core with spongy cover suggested" - PM said "odd shaped, with a spongy cover", nothing heart-shaped
"UI Designer (UL Hazred)" - the name given is Abdul al-Hasred
"Light turns on with motion sensor" stated as fact; it was only debated, and continuous light on power-on was also floated
Action item "Facilitate discussion on wheel sensor necessity" and "Assess cost implications of wheel sensor" were never assigned; the wheel was kept
Action item "Develop banana-shaped spongy case design" assigned to Industrial Designer alone is not stated; PM asked ID and UI designer to work together
"Provide meeting notes in shared folder" - PM said notes would be in his folder, a minor paraphrase stretch
Several timestamps do not match (e.g. final look and feel at 21:40, action items at 20:26)
strengths: Captures the wheel sensor 50x cost and the 12 euro budget
Records the plastic cover objections and the left/right hand discussion
Notes the prototype collaboration between industrial and UI designers
weaknesses: Omits the voice recognition chip email entirely
Does not clearly state that the wheel was decided to be kept despite cost
Action items list is padded with invented tasks
Recap of prior decisions is mixed into 'Design Decisions' as if new

evaluations.label: B
errors: "Alternative: recess or offset channel buttons slightly" - 'recess' is not said; UI designer only said put them a bit out of the way
"Backlit buttons confirmed" slightly overstates; lighting was carried over and referenced, but trigger and battery questions were left open
Next steps split work as 'Industrial designer to produce final banana-form design' and 'UI designer to finalize layout', an inferred split of what PM assigned jointly
strengths: Clear recap of previous meeting decisions including no LCD/voice
States wheel kept despite ~50x cost, with the reasons and the 12 euro ceiling
Covers voice recognition chip update and that the decision was deferred
Covers banana choice with reasons, construction with spongy cover, and left/right handedness resolution
Well organized and easy to act on
weaknesses: Omits the push-down wheel idea and that further instructions come by email
No owners attached to evaluation step

evaluations.label: C
errors: "IS1001c remote control" - this project code never appears in the transcript
"an arched internal structure for component mounting" - 'arched' is invented
"backlit buttons that activate upon movement" presented as a specification; activation method was debated and not decided
"Will adding motion sensors ... exceed the target production cost of 12 euros" frames an open question nobody raised in that form
"Action Items (none)" - PM asked ID and UI designer to collaborate on the prototype and said instructions would follow by email
Uses inconsistent labels ('UIZ', 'Speaker 1-4') that make attribution unclear
strengths: Covers voice recognition chip, wheel cost, plastic cover rejection, wheel push-down, and market priorities
Outline section follows the meeting flow well
weaknesses: Contains invented details (project code, arched structure)
Action items section empty despite clear assignments
Speaker labels are confusing for someone who missed the meeting

evaluations.label: D
errors: "channel wheel, preview button" - transcript says previous channel button
"The group kept the wheel ... [11:04]" - at that point PM only suggested it might be an advantage; the decision to keep it came around 15:54
"The wheel could be pressed down to recall a channel" - UI designer said push-down could be used 'for the record'; 'recall a channel' is an interpretation
"The group did not document a detailed resolution" on left/right use - PM argued it works for both hands and UI designer accepted 'Okay. Maybe.'
strengths: Accurate on wheel cost (50x), 12 euro budget, lighting debate and battery concern
Covers voice recognition chip and that no decision was made
Captures banana choice reasons including company colour scheme and findability
States the prototype collaboration, next work items, and email instructions
weaknesses: Action items section is empty; tasks only appear in body
Summary repeats points; some timestamps misplaced
Plastic cover outcome is not stated as a decision

rationale: B is the most accurate and complete, with a clear recap, decisions with reasons, the deferred voice chip question, and next steps. D is accurate and thorough with good timestamps but has small errors (preview button, wheel decision timing) and an empty action items section. C covers most topics and lists open questions but invents a project code and an 'arched' structure, states motion-activated lighting as decided, and lists no action items. A misses the voice chip, invents a 'heart-shaped' core, misspells the name, and pads action items with tasks nobody was given.
